name: C++
note: clang++ compiles each C++ controller into its own program (ADR 0099). A controller is one header-only class in server/controllers, and its markers are standard attributes: `class [[RequestRoute("/orders")]] [[Public]] OrdersController` and `[[GetRoute]]` on the method declare GET /orders. A parameter says where its value comes from with `[[FromPath]]`, `[[FromQuery]]`, `[[FromBody]]`, `[[FromHeader]]` or `[[FromCookie]]`. One parameter may have no marker: `const tachyon::http::HttpRequestMessage& request` receives the whole request. The method returns a value: `bool`, a number, `std::string`, `std::vector`, `std::optional`, `tachyon::json::JsonNode` or a model from server/models, and Tachyon writes it as JSON with status 200. `void` and an empty `std::optional` answer 204. `[[ResponseStatus(201)]]` sets another success status. A method that returns `tachyon::http::HttpResponseMessage` sets the status, headers and body itself. Tachyon writes the JSON code of every model, because C++ has no reflection. A controller reaches the services and helpers in server/services and server/helpers through reference fields such as `[[Needs]] OrderService& orders;`, and they may use Lifetime, OnStart, OnStop and OnEvent. A worker in server/workers is a `class Handler` with a `POST()` method and an optional `[[Schedule({...})]]`. A Setup in server/setups opens a behavior context, and `[[Settings]]` and `[[Setting]]` models in server/models bind the private snapshot. A `[[Checked]]` struct in server/models declares field rules with Required, NotEmpty, Length, Min and Max, and `[[Check]]` on a service or route parameter of that type checks the value before the method runs: a broken rule answers 422 with `application/problem+json` (ADR 0101). A `[[Converter]]` class in server/converters declares methods without a body, and Tachyon writes each mapping; a controller or service asks for it with `[[Needs]] ProductConverter& converter;`. An `[[ErrorHandler]]` class in server/controllers turns an error type from server/errors into an answer, and an `[[IdentityProvider]]` class says who is signed in. A C++ controller has no stores, HTTP clients, middleware, streams, sockets, relays, gateways or test units yet: their markers stop the build (most with TY1308) and the message says that C++ gets them in a later step.
